top_story.headline: Air Force plans $1.5 million in "Outward Mindset" leadership training from the Arbinger Institute with no competition
top_story.dek: The justification says only the Arbinger Institute can supply its proprietary courses for about 900 leaders at the Ogden Air Logistics Complex and two outposts.
paragraphs: The Air Force's Ogden Air Logistics Complex at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to set up a single-award blanket purchase agreement with The Arbinger Institute (also called The Arbinger Company) for leadership training. The justification's cover page gives an estimated contract cost, including options, of $1,500,000, while its narrative describes a five-year ordering period, from about February 15, 2027 to February 14, 2032, with "an estimated total ceiling of $3M". The justification invokes the only-one-responsible-source authority and describes the courses as proprietary. It was posted as a Special Notice rather than under the Justification category.

The requirement covers about 900 leaders and key personnel at the complex and at two outposts, the Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, Arizona, and the 575th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron at Randolph Air Force Base, Texas. The courses are Developing and Implementing an Outward Mindset, Outward Leadership and Outward Performance, plus train-the-trainer certifications. The document calls the certification pathway "a key component" meant to build a self-sustaining internal training capacity.

The document also says the complex "previously attempted to remove barriers to competition by having internal personnel facilitate courses modeled on the Arbinger concept." USAspending shows a federal contract under Arbinger's name going back to December 2018, so this is not its first government work.

sections.eyebrow: White House & Executive Office of the President
sections.headline: Navy plans to buy Marine One's fiscal 2028 spare parts from Sikorsky without competition
paragraphs: Two combined synopsis/solicitations are tagged White House today: a Navy spare-parts buy for the presidential helicopter and an Army off-road vehicle purchase delivered for the White House Military Office. A third tagged notice, a V-22 flight-control retrofit, went back to Combined Synopsis/Solicitations because its visible text does not mention the presidential fleet.

blocks.title: Navy plans to buy fiscal 2028 spare parts for the presidential helicopter from Sikorsky without competition
meta: other than full and open competition
blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command says it will negotiate a delivery order, and later modifications, under Basic Ordering Agreement N00019-23-G-0002 with Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation, a Lockheed Martin company, for fiscal 2028 spare parts and rapid parts procurements for the VH-92A, the Marine One helicopter. The notice follows a January 6, 2025 sources sought notice that drew two responses, which the Navy says it adjudicated. It describes Sikorsky as the only known source with the needed knowledge and experience (the posted text is cut off after that). No dollar value is posted, and the one attachment has not been read yet.

blocks.title: Army shops for a Polaris Xpedition off-road vehicle delivered to Fort Myer for the White House Military Office
blocks.text: The Army's Mission and Installation Contracting Command office at Fort Drum is seeking a new Polaris XPEDITION ADV 5 NorthStar in a neutral black or grey, five seats, enclosed cabin, 999-1000cc twin-cylinder engine, 4,500-pound winch and heating and air conditioning. The notice, titled "Side by Side Offroad," calls for delivery to Fort Myer, Virginia and labels the vehicle delivery "(White House Military Office)". No price or quantity is posted.

sections.headline: Navy holds a closed-to-media maritime industry day in Washington on December 8
paragraphs: Three items stay in this section: one special notice, one award notice and one sources sought notice. Four other tagged items went back to their home sections because the capital appeared only in a contracting office's name or the work is elsewhere: a $108.9 million Suitland, Maryland lab award, a $45 million Annapolis, Maryland energy plan, a nationwide Health and Human Services security contract, and a Japan tugboat repair.

blocks.title: Navy's maritime acquisition office will brief industry in Washington, D.C. at an event closed to the press
blocks.text: The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime office, which the notice says is responsible for aircraft carrier, surface, expeditionary, mine warfare and auxiliary fleet ship construction and sustainment, is hosting its Fall 2026 Industry Day in person in Washington, D.C. Leadership will give portfolio updates and "highlight upcoming contracting opportunities." The notice states plainly: "This event is closed to media attendance."
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Marine Corps books 180 Westin Times Square rooms for $754,920 without competition for Army-Navy Week
paragraphs: There are 25 new justifications, 13 of them posted under other notice types, and none repeat earlier editions. One is today's Top Story (the Arbinger Institute training buy) and six are in Extensions, leaving 18 here. Nothing else is as unusual, but a no-bid hotel block, a fuel spot buy and a mobile-lab rental are worth reading.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Marine Corps books 180 rooms at the Westin Times Square for Army-Navy Week without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Marine Corps plans to lodge 180 Marines and civilians in New York City for six nights, December 7-13, 2026, during Army-Navy Week. The justification, posted as a Special Notice, says the Westin Times Square is "the only responsible source identified capable of providing the requested accommodations at the level of support required." It is a hotel stay bought by a military service without a competition, which is unusual.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency's fuel arm justifies three urgent Western Pacific fuel purchases from BP after the fact
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy awarded three spot-buy purchase orders (SPE60226P0470, P0471 and P0472) to BP Products North America Inc. on May 1, 2026 for petroleum products for Western Pacific locations. The justification says it was "approved and publicized after award" because preparing it beforehand "would have unreasonably delayed the acquisition." It says market research found BP's Cherry Point Refinery was the only offeror able to deliver within the required window by tanker. Values are blacked out.

blocks.title: Amarillo veterans hospital rents its lab trailers from Lab-Pro without competition after the earlier contract was terminated for default
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Amarillo VA Healthcare System needs two mobile laboratory modules (a trailer with a cleanroom) while its lab is under construction. Per the justification, Lab-Pro, Inc. supplied them as a subcontractor under construction contract 36C25722C0093, which "was terminated for default in May 2026." Because the trailer is connected to the hospital's electrical, fire-suppression and water systems, the document argues that switching vendors would stop patient testing. The linked award notice lists $374,879 on October 15, above the justification's estimate. USAspending's earliest contract under Lab-Pro's name carries that same date.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Veterans Affairs bridges Providence valet parking to incumbent VetPride after a protest forced it to cancel a new award
paragraphs: Six new justifications keep an incumbent running: one bridge after a Government Accountability Office protest, a NASA lease, a prison medical contract and three smaller renewals.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs gives incumbent VetPride a no-bid valet parking bridge in Providence after a protest forced it to cancel the new award
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: A post-award protest filed August 7, 2026 (docketed B-424728.1) challenged contract 36C24127P0001, awarded July 30. The agency chose to terminate it, revise the evaluation factor and re-evaluate, and the Government Accountability Office dismissed the protest September 14. The bridge for VetPride Services, LLC, incumbent under contract 36C24122C0001, is a three-month base, a three-month option and up to six months under FAR 52.217-8. The prior contract was to expire September 30, 2026. The award record is dated October 1 and shows $0.

blocks.title: NASA keeps a launch pad repair team in its Kennedy Space Center trailer through a no-bid lease from United Rental
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: NASA will lease a modular trailer for 12 months for the Kennedy Space Center construction management and corrosion control team. The justification says NASA is "realigning their contract infrastructure with the Administration's direction," so the capability that provided access to the facility "is being removed" and falls to NASA "on very short notice." The team is doing launch damage refurbishment on the pad for Artemis III, and NASA says it intends to compete the capability after next fiscal year. As written, the document's lease dates run from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026.

blocks.title: Bureau of Prisons continues NaphCare's inmate medical services at its Petersburg prison complex without competition for $555,000
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Prisons says that as incumbent, NaphCare Inc. agreed to keep providing comprehensive medical services for the Federal Correctional Complex in Hopewell, Virginia at its prior Medicare benchmark rates. The justification says NaphCare has served the institution for over five years and that moving to a new provider would require 30 to 60 days of security clearances and service start-up.

items: General Services Administration extends an Englewood, Colorado office lease for 60 months without competition. The current lease expires January 31, 2028, and the value is redacted. (5CO0518)

Veterans Affairs continues preventive maintenance of 50-plus ceiling patient lifts at Tuscaloosa VA Medical Center with Savaria Concord Lifts and Handicare USA without competition. It was posted as an Award Notice and the value is redacted. (36C24726P0797)
Veterans Affairs keeps Comcast cable television running in White River Junction patient areas without competition. It was posted as a Special Notice with no value stated. (36C24127Q0038)

sections.headline: Navy gives Consigli Construction $108.9 million to build a foreign materiel intelligence lab in Suitland, Maryland
paragraphs: There are 50 new award notices, with 2 repeats left out. One more award, a Defense Information Systems Agency circuit, is in the Washington, D.C. section.

blocks.title: Navy gives Consigli Construction $108.9 million to build its Foreign Materiel Exploitation Laboratory in Suitland, Maryland
blocks.text: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command's Washington office awarded Consigli Construction Co., Inc. a design-build task order on October 22 under contract N4008023D0028. The project is P-664, the Foreign Materiel Exploitation Laboratory at the National Maritime Intelligence Center in Suitland, Maryland. The notice gives no further description.

blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command awarded The Boeing Company contract N0001927D1006 on October 16, 2026, an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract for MQ-25 software, on a sole-source basis. This is the award notice for a solicitation listed earlier today. The attachment has not been read yet.

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency's Pacific fuel bid bars any offer that routes through the Strait of Hormuz
paragraphs: There are 156 new solicitations, with 2 repeats left out and 23 flagged by screening. Many are amendments to solicitations listed earlier and are omitted.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency's Pacific bulk fuel solicitation bars any offer that requires transit through the Strait of Hormuz
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy's Western Pacific Bulk Fuels Purchase Program (SPE602-26-R-0706) adds to its price evaluation: "No offers will be evaluated that require vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz." The conformed solicitation lists estimated quantities of 183,560,000 gallons of F-76 naval distillate, 265,540,000 of Jet A-1 and 130,774,000 of JP-5. The agency's emergency BP fuel spot buys are in Sole-Source Justifications.

blocks.title: State Department pushes its passport printer bid deadline to November 2027
blocks.text: The Department of State revised the closing date for Next Generation Passport Personalization Printers Support (19AQMM24R0113) to November 30, 2027, from October 30, 2026. The notice lists at least eight closing-date revisions since March 16, 2026. Its 22 attachments have not been read yet.

blocks.title: Federal health agency seeks vaccine makers for the pandemic influenza stockpile
meta: Department of Health and Human Services
blocks.text: The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority issued a request for proposals to continue its vaccine medical countermeasures for pandemic influenza. It covers vaccines, antigens and adjuvants (with U.S. facilities preferred) and support for rapid regulatory work. Its 26 attachments are queued unread.

sections.headline: Navy plans a lifetime purchase of obsolete F/A-18 targeting-processor electronics from Boeing without competition
paragraphs: There are 124 new combined synopsis/solicitations, with 367 repeats left out and 9 flagged by screening. Three others are in the White House section or came back from it.

blocks.title: Navy plans a lifetime purchase of obsolete F/A-18 targeting-processor electronics from Boeing without competition
blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command intends to issue a firm-fixed-price delivery order to The Boeing Company under sole-source Basic Ordering Agreement N0001926G1002. It is a Life of Type Buy of obsolete electronic components for the Distributed Targeting Processor-Networked on the F/A-18 and EA-18G. Performance is to begin in August 2027, and the notice calls Boeing the only known firm with the needed expertise.

items: Navy advertises engineering services to support ASTARS as a sole-source requirement. The posted text names no vendor or value. (N00421-27-SIMACQ-AN10000-AN1000M-0016)
Defense Threat Reduction Agency seeks a small business to destroy IT storage devices at its Reston, Virginia facility. (HDTRA127Q0003)
Army Corps of Engineers Omaha District seeks fuel tank inspections at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The deadline moved to November 13. (W9128F27QA002)
Norfolk Naval Shipyard plans a no-bid retrofit kit for two HPAC units from RIX Industries. A document read today on a notice posted earlier shows this. (N4215827QS0002)

blocks.text: Returned from the White House tag, listed earlier today: Naval Air Systems Command's sole-source V-22 flight control retrofit order to BAE Systems Controls (N0001927R0005). sections.headline: Navy plans a $45 million no-bid energy plant at Naval Support Activity Annapolis with Baltimore Gas and Electric
paragraphs: There are 57 new presolicitations, with 17 repeats left out and 11 flagged by screening. One Washington-office item moved here from the D.C. tag.

blocks.title: Navy plans a $45 million no-bid power plant and microgrid at Naval Support Activity Annapolis with Baltimore Gas and Electric
blocks.text: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command intends to award a Utility Energy Service Contract to Baltimore Gas and Electric Company for design, construction, commissioning and financing at Naval Support Activity Annapolis, Maryland. The plan has a combined heat and power plant supporting an estimated 19 megawatts of peak demand with three natural gas turbines and a microgrid that can run in island mode during grid outages.

blocks.title: Navy plans a no-bid production order for BAE Systems' digital interrogator
blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command intends to award a sole-source cost-plus-fixed-fee order under Basic Ordering Agreement N0001922G0009 to BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration, Inc. of Greenlawn, New York. It covers production of the AN/UPX-52 Common Core Digital Interrogator, moving from lab-built prototypes to factory production, with test equipment and a re-spin option.

items: Navy plans a sole-source buy of submarine hydraulic manifolds and valves from Sargent Aerospace & Defense. It cites 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). (N64498-26-RFPREQ-PD-45-0004)
Coast Guard plans a service-disabled veteran set-aside to repair storm sewer lines at its San Juan, Puerto Rico base. (DB-PNUM15852459)

blocks.text: Not written up because they were listed earlier today: F-47 Nellis campus, Collins CH-53K software, USNS John Lenthall deactivation, submarine emergency diesel generator renewal, Coast Guard housing and lighthouse repairs. Routine: Defense Logistics Agency Aviation offices 11 and Navy weapon systems support 3.

sections.headline: Vandenberg Space Force Base facility contract shifts to an 8(a) set-aside as launches are projected to reach 1,800 a year
paragraphs: There are 38 new special notices, with 2 repeats left out and 8 flagged by screening. One more, the Navy industry day, is in the D.C. section.

blocks.title: Vandenberg facility maintenance follow-on goes to 8(a) firms as the Air Force projects a 27-fold rise in launches
blocks.text: A briefing for the Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution contract says "65 launches in 2025 will increase to approximately 1,800 by 2036" at Vandenberg Space Force Base, which it describes as 184 square miles with over 2,000 buildings. A question-and-answer spreadsheet says the follow-on is "100% 8(a) Set-Aside" where it earlier said small-business set-aside, to reach firms with relevant past performance. The files were posted October 8.

items: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services bans commercial AI tools and bots from its October 27 industry day. The notice says such "bots or unknown callers" will be removed. (USCISFY27CONFERENCECALL1stQUARTER)

Commerce Department relays a NATO ballistic missile defense battle management bid for U.S. firms with Secret facility clearances. The NATO Communications and Information Agency is the buyer. (CO-423316-RTBMD)
Air Force Hanscom base sets up an Other Transaction framework to attract builders with little federal experience. (HERO-FY27)

blocks.text: Not written up: Fort Bragg joint deployment complex, fighter engine industry day, Navy software defined radio, Seattle Sentinel industry day (listed earlier). Routine: NASA 4, Army Mobile District 2, others singly.

sections.headline: No featured USAspending contract actions today
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.
The data showed no new awards of $2 million or more, no large modifications and no cuts.

blocks.text: Under $2 million: one new award was screened, from the Defense Department backlog, and none was flagged.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files were approved in this window
paragraphs: No new OMB apportionment notices have been published since October 21. The routine apportionments monitored across federal agencies remain unchanged.

footer.coverage_window: October 26, 2026 (Pacific time), afternoon edition, covering SAM.gov postings and attached documents through the afternoon.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API (morning edition only); SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. USAspending is pulled in the morning edition only and carried over here. OMB Apportionments found no new files since October 21. Of 1,549 attachments on 339 notices, 1,049 are queued for later editions, 108 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 1 could not be downloaded; 4,430 files overall are queued, so findings may surface later. About 309 links to outside portals were not followed. Several items written up above have unread attachments, including the Marine One spare-parts notice.
